Reagan, Dodds, Danforth et al. (2016), \.Man in a hole (fall, then rise): The protagonist encounters trouble, reaches a low point, and recovers.
Reagan, Dodds, Danforth et al. (2016), \.Icarus (rise, then fall): Success or happiness increases before ending in collapse.
Reagan, Dodds, Danforth et al. (2016), \.Cinderella (rise, fall, then rise): Improvement is interrupted by a major reversal, followed by recovery or triumph.
Reagan, Dodds, Danforth et al. (2016), \.Oedipus (fall, rise, then fall): Initial misfortune is followed by recovery, then a final deterioration.

Redemption sequences.Sacrifice: Suffering endured for a valued good

Contamination sequences.Failure: Hope or effort culminates in defeat

Interpretive features.Meaning-making: Events are assigned lessons or significance
Interpretive features.Positive resolution: Tension ends in an adaptive conclusion

Narrative coherence.Temporal coherence: Events are ordered clearly in time
Narrative coherence.Causal coherence: Events are linked through cause and consequence
Narrative coherence.Thematic coherence: Episodes are unified by recurring meanings
Narrative coherence.Cultural coherence: The story follows recognizable cultural scripts

Broader life-story configuration.The redemptive self: A life organized around transforming suffering into growth and contribution

Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Supplication: A powerless person appeals to an uncertain authority for protection from a persecutor.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Deliverance: A rescuer saves an unfortunate person from danger or punishment.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Crime Pursued by Vengeance: An avenger pursues someone who has committed an inadequately punished crime.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Vengeance Taken for Kindred upon Kindred: One relative avenges a wrong committed by another relative against their shared kin.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Pursuit: A fugitive is hunted for an alleged or actual offense.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Disaster: A powerful person or institution is defeated, ruined, or overthrown.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Falling Prey to Cruelty or Misfortune: A relatively helpless person suffers under an oppressor or impersonal calamity.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Revolt: A conspirator or rebel challenges a tyrannical power.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Daring Enterprise: A bold leader attempts to obtain something difficult from a formidable adversary.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Abduction: Someone is taken away from the person or power responsible for protecting them.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.The Enigma: A seeker must solve a problem, mystery, or riddle posed by an interrogator.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Obtaining: Someone attempts to acquire a desired person, object, privilege, or decision from a resisting party.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Enmity of Kinsmen: Members of the same family hate, persecute, or destroy one another.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Rivalry of Kinsmen: Relatives compete for the same person, possession, status, or affection.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Murderous Adultery: Adulterous lovers plot the death of the betrayed spouse.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Madness: A person under the influence of insanity harms an innocent victim.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Fatal Imprudence: Negligence, rashness, ignorance, or misplaced confidence causes grave harm.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Involuntary Crimes of Love: Lovers unknowingly enter a forbidden or incestuous relationship.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Slaying of a Kinsman Unrecognized: Someone unknowingly kills a relative or loved one whose identity is concealed.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Self-Sacrifice for an Ideal: A person gives up life, welfare, possessions, or relationships for a principle or cause.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Self-Sacrifice for Kindred: A person sacrifices themselves or something precious for a relative.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.All Sacrificed for a Passion: A consuming passion causes someone to abandon duty, fortune, family, reputation, or life.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Necessity of Sacrificing Loved Ones: Duty, survival, religion, or necessity compels someone to sacrifice a loved one.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Rivalry of Superior and Inferior: Unequal rivals compete for the same object, person, or position.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Adultery: A spouse is betrayed through a secret relationship.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Crimes of Love: Love itself violates a social, familial, religious, or moral prohibition.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Discovery of the Dishonor of a Loved One: Someone discovers that a loved or respected person has committed a shameful act.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Obstacles to Love: Two lovers are separated or opposed by external circumstances.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.An Enemy Loved: Someone falls in love with a person whom they, their family, or their community are expected to hate.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Ambition: A person pursues power, rank, wealth, or achievement against an opposing force.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Conflict with a God: A mortal struggles against a deity, fate, divine law, or supernatural power.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Mistaken Jealousy: False evidence or manipulation causes someone to suspect a loved one of betrayal.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Erroneous Judgment: An innocent person is condemned or harmed because the judge misunderstands the facts.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Remorse: A wrongdoer is psychologically or morally tormented by a past act.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Recovery of a Lost One: A seeker locates, rescues, or is reunited with someone who disappeared.
Georges Polti, \"The Thirty-Six Dramatic.Loss of Loved Ones: A person witnesses or experiences the death of a loved one, often through another’s actions.

Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.Overcoming the Monster: The protagonist confronts and defeats a threatening, often overwhelmingly powerful antagonist.
Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.Rags to Riches: An obscure, poor, or disregarded protagonist gains success, status, maturity, or recognition—often after temporarily losing it.
Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.The Quest: The protagonist and companions undertake a difficult journey to obtain a goal, overcoming successive obstacles and temptations.
Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.Voyage and Return: The protagonist enters an unfamiliar world, experiences its wonders and dangers, and eventually returns with greater understanding.
Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.Comedy: A community becomes entangled in confusion, misunderstanding, disguise, or frustrated relationships before the disorder is resolved in reconciliation and union. Booker uses “comedy” structurally, not simply to mean humorous fiction.
Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.Tragedy: A central character is drawn toward destruction through a flaw, obsession, temptation, or increasingly wrongful choices.
Christopher Booker, \"The Seven Basic Pl.Rebirth: The protagonist falls under a dark, frozen, corrupted, or spiritually dead condition and is ultimately restored through a redemptive influence.
